title: Energy modeling specialist
description: You are a building energy modeling specialist. You have 3 to 7 years of hands-on experience running full building energy simulations and you know the difference between a well-built model and a model that simply runs. You take modeling seriously and your work product reflects it. You are an IES VE expert. IES Virtual Environment is your primary simulation tool. You know it deeply: you can build geometry from scratch, assign constructions, configure HVAC systems, set up occupancy and lighting profiles, run compliance checks, and interpret results. You do not need to be trained on IES VE. You know ASHRAE 90.1-2022 inside and out. You have applied both the Energy Cost Budget (ECB) method and the Performance Rating Method (PRM) on real projects. You understand the mandatory requirements, prescriptive path, and how the compliance pathways differ and when each applies. You are proficient in the 2024 IECC. You understand the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code commercial provisions including the mandatory requirements, prescriptive compliance path, and Energy Rating Index (ERI) compliance options. You can navigate Section C401 through C408 without looking everything up. You understand building systems at a technical level. Envelope assemblies, U-values, SHGC, infiltration rates, HVAC system types and efficiencies, lighting power densities, and plug loads are part of your everyday vocabulary. You know how modeling assumptions affect results. You are a strong communicator. You write and speak English at a professional level. You can explain complex energy model results to engineers, architects, and clients in a way that is accurate and understandable. This is a requirement, not a preference. You are detail-oriented and self-directed. You catch your own errors before they become client-facing problems. You manage your time, meet deadlines, and produce deliverables that do not require extensive rework. WHAT YOU WILL DO Perform complete building energy simulations using IES VE for new construction, major renovation, and retrofit projects across multiple building types including Healthcare, Mission Critical, Higher Education, and Government facilities. Conduct ASHRAE 90.1-2022 compliance modeling using both the Energy Cost Budget (ECB) method and the Performance Rating Method (PRM). Document the baseline building configuration, proposed design, and performance results in accordance with the standard. Perform 2024 IECC commercial energy compliance analysis including mandatory requirements review, prescriptive path compliance verification, and trade-off calculations. Produce compliance documentation suitable for submittal to authorities having jurisdiction (AHJ). Model all major building systems within IES VE including building envelope assemblies (walls, roofs, floors, fenestration), HVAC systems (air-side and water-side), domestic hot water, lighting systems, plug loads, and on-site renewable energy where applicable. Evaluate energy conservation measures (ECMs) through parametric modeling. Run multiple design scenarios, compare results, and provide clear recommendations with supporting data to help clients and design teams make informed decisions. Collaborate with commissioning engineers to compare modeled system performance against installed equipment schedules and sequences of operation. Identify discrepancies and support the commissioning process with energy-based analysis. Coordinate with project architects and MEP engineers of record to obtain accurate model inputs including construction assemblies, equipment schedules, ventilation rates, and occupancy data. Document all assumptions clearly and maintain an assumption log for each project. Prepare clear, professional energy model reports documenting methodology, inputs, results, and conclusions. Reports must be suitable for client delivery and regulatory submittal. Support Building Envelope Commissioning (BECx) efforts with thermal bridging analysis, condensation risk review, and energy impact assessment of envelope performance gaps. Stay current with code updates, standard revisions, and software developments. As ASHRAE standards and energy codes evolve, you will be expected to adapt modeling practices accordingly. POSITION REQUIREMENTS Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Building Science, or a closely related field (required) 3 to 7 years of hands-on building energy modeling experience on real construction projects (required) Proficiency in IES Virtual Environment (IES VE) is required and nonnegotiable. Candidates who do not have demonstrated IES VE experience will not be considered. INTERVIEW REQUIREMENT: All candidates must present a minimum of two completed IES VE energy models during the interview. Candidates will be expected to walk through their modeling approach, explain key assumptions, identify compliance outcomes, and answer detailed technical questions about the models. Presenting borrowed or template models is grounds for immediate disqualification. POSITION REQUIREMENTS -Demonstrated proficiency in ASHRAE 90.1-2022 including ECB method, PRM compliance pathway, mandatory provisions, and envelope and mechanical system requirements -Demonstrated proficiency in 2024 IECC commercial energy provisions including mandatory requirements, prescriptive compliance, and trade-off compliance paths -Familiarity with EnergyPlus or DOE-2 simulation engines is a plus -Exceptional English proficiency, written and verbal, at a professional business level (required, nonnegotiable) -Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite including Word, Excel, and Outlook -Must be available to work hours that overlap with US Central Time (CST) business hours on a consistent, daily basis -Full time position, minimum 40 hours per week

title: Total Video Editing Genius
description: The McCord List Media Network | Faith-Forward, Female-Founded, Nationally Syndicated ----- **Employment type: Starting at PT, but will quickly grow if this is the right fit **Hours:**  8-3pm PST ----- ## Read this part first We are not looking for someone who “does some editing.” We are looking for a total crusher. Someone who opens Premiere Pro and disappears into the work. Someone who turns raw footage into broadcast-ready episodes without being chased, watches the full cut before anyone has to ask, and treats a missed deadline like a personal offense. If you need hand-holding, this is not your role. If you have been waiting for a place that moves as fast as you do, keep reading. The McCord List Media Network is a nationally syndicated media operation reaching more than 90 million households across Roku, Amazon Prime, Samsung TV Plus, and Tubi. We produce The McCord List Today plus a growing roster of client shows, all from a real LED soundstage in Manhattan Beach. We are faith-led, purpose-driven, and obsessed with editorial polish. Every frame we publish carries the brand. This is a high-volume, high-standards seat. The right person will thrive on it. ----- ## What you will own You are the engine room of our content. Your job is to take raw footage and turn it into polished, on-brand, broadcast-ready episodes and the social clips that fuel our reach. Week to week, you will: - Pull and organize weekly raw footage from our Google Drive client folders by filming date, and confirm intro, outro, branding, and guest assets are in place before you cut - Edit full-length episodes in Adobe Premiere Pro: clean cuts, balanced audio, color and LUTs applied, awkward host ---------- nts and BTS removed, branded intro and outro graphics in place - Export final episodes in high resolution (both our 22-minute and 40 to 48 minute formats) and file them correctly under Final Episodes - Cut individual interview segments for each guest - Generate 30 to 35 social clips per episode in Opus Clip Pro, then review every clip for accuracy, brand tone, captions, logo, and framing before it ships - Maintain clean, standardized folder structure in Google Drive so nothing ever gets lost - Upload approved episodes to U Screen with complete, accurate metadata pulled from the Content Sheet (title, guests, description, SEO, category) - Keep the task sheet and dashboard current on every episode, and flag missing assets or technical issues immediately - Move episodes through our review chain: edit, submit to Nicole, apply notes, host review, final revisions, approved, posted - Jump on special projects when leadership calls: sizzle reels, highlight cuts, promo overlays, urgent social turnarounds ----- ## The numbers (this is the filter) We say crusher and we mean it. Here is the pace: - **8 to 10 episodes per week** combined across The McCord List Today and client shows - Roughly **3 episodes** for The McCord List Today and **7** for client shows - Every edit delivered within **24 to 48 hours** of raw footage delivery - **30 to 35 social clips** generated and reviewed per episode If those numbers excite you instead of scaring you, we should talk. ----- ## The quality bar We do not ship anything that does not look and sound like us. Every deliverable is checked against our QA standard before it goes out: - Clean, balanced audio throughout - Bumpers in place (first, middle, end) and the correct intro and outro sizzle - Names and titles spelled correctly - Nothing distracting in the background and no stray BTS left in - Correct brand logo, every time - Social clips with accurate captions, the brand logo, and the host or guest centered in frame - Consistent file naming: `Episode [#] - Guest Name - Final.mp4` You will be the last line of defense on quality. That is a responsibility we hand to people who take it seriously. ----- ## You are a fit if you - Live inside Adobe Premiere Pro and edit fast without sacrificing polish - Have a real eye for pacing, color, and audio, and you notice the small things other editors miss - Are fluent (or fast to learn) in Opus Clip, U Screen, Envato Elements, and Google Drive based workflows - Manage your own queue, hit deadlines without reminders, and communicate proactively when something is off - Understand brand consistency and protect it like it is your name on the export - Have published work for streaming, broadcast, or high-volume digital content (please send your reel) - Can troubleshoot audio issues and care about presenting work that crushes the game ## Bonus points if you - Have worked in a fast-paced media network, agency, or studio environment - Know your way around motion graphics and templated branded packages - Care about purpose-driven, faith-forward content and want your work to mean something ----- ## Why this seat You will be part of a media network that is scaling, not stalling. Your edits go out to tens of millions of households, not into a folder no one opens. You will work alongside a tight, driven team that values craft, speed, and faith. And you will see your fingerprints on a brand that is building something rare in this industry. We are looking for one person who wants to crush it here for the long run. ----- ## How to apply Send the following: 1. Your reel or a link to 2 to 3 recent full edits you are proud of 1. A short note on the highest volume you have ever sustained and how you kept quality high 1. The fastest you have ever turned a polished episode from raw footage No generic cover letters. Show us the work. ----- *The McCord List Media Network is a division of LaunchPreneur, Inc.*

description: About Us We're a multi-brand DTC e-commerce company doing ~$300K/month. We run paid ads on Meta at scale and we're growing fast. We're not an agency. We own our brands. That means when you write a winning ad, you see the spend scale, the ROAS climb, and the brand grow. Your work has real impact and you stay with us long-term. We're hiring ONE Creative Strategist to work directly with the founder. This is a long-term role, not a project. If you want stability, growth, and to actually OWN the creative output of a real brand, keep reading. What You'll Actually Do You are the engine behind every ad we run. You research, you think, you write, and you brief our editors. The editors execute YOUR ideas. You will: Write hooks, ad concepts, and short-form scripts (15s, 30s, 60s, and longer VSL formats) Develop angles — new mechanisms, new avatars, new pain points, new positioning we haven't tested yet Mine customer reviews, comments, and competitor ads to find winning insights and translate them into ads Brief our video editors with clear, executable creative briefs (we'll teach you our brief format) Analyze ad performance and tell us what to double down on, what to iterate, what to kill Build creative variations from winners — take one winning ad and turn it into 10–20 meaningful variations Research customer psychology using reviews from Amazon, Trustpilot, Reddit, and our own product pages Manage the creative pipeline in Google Sheets / Notion (briefs, deadlines, asset tracking, performance) Stay on top of competitor activity — what new ads are running, what offers are tested, what's scaling The founder will work alongside you on strategy. But you own the creative output. If our ads suck, that's on you. If they win, that's on you too — and we pay accordingly. Who This Is For You are right for this role if: You have at least 1 year of hands-on experience writing ads, hooks, and concepts for DTC or e-commerce brands. Not just "social media posts." Direct response paid ads. You can show us ads you wrote that ran on Meta or TikTok with real spend behind them You speak fluent written English and your writing has voice, rhythm, and persuasion — not robotic AI output You're obsessed with customer psychology. You actually enjoy reading 100 reviews to find the one phrase that becomes the hook. You're organized to a fault. Briefs go out on time, files named properly, sheets updated daily. You can write FAST. A new hook in 10 minutes, not 2 hours. A full 30s script in 30 minutes. You want to learn DTC marketing at a high level over 1–2 years and grow with one company. You can work 30–40 hours/week consistently. You are NOT right for this role if: You're a graphic designer, video editor, or general VA looking to pivot. This is a writer + strategist role. You write generic "benefit list" ads. We need angles, hooks, narratives — not bullet points. You can't show real ads you wrote. Portfolio is mandatory. You're using AI to write your application but couldn't defend your own answer live on a call. You want to run 5 client gigs on the side. We need focus. Compensation Hourly: $5–8/hour depending on experience and portfolio strength Hours: 30–40 hrs/week (full-time) Schedule: Flexible. Some overlap with European hours required (5 hours/day minimum overlap). Performance bonus: After 90 days, you earn a bonus every time one of your ads scales past a spend threshold at positive ROAS. Real money on top of base. We pay extra for winners. Growth path: Strong performers move to $7–10/hour within 6 months and own a full brand inside the company within 12 months. We pay on time. Every time. How to Apply (Read Carefully — Most Applicants Will Skip This) We get a lot of AI-generated applications. We can spot them in 10 seconds and we delete them. Here's what we actually want: 1. Put the word "octopus" as the first word of your application. This tells us you read the post. 2. Pick ONE ad fro ---------- ta Ad Library (www.> >facebook .com /ads/library) — any DTC brand, any niche. Then answer in your own words (NOT ChatGPT): a) What is the hook in the first 3 seconds and why does it work? b) Who is the target customer (avatar) and what is the main pain point or desire being triggered? c) Write 3 alternate hooks you would test against this ad. Real hooks, written out as you would write them for a script. d) What angle would you test next to improve performance (new avatar, new mechanism, new positioning)? Keep it tight. 200–300 words total. We care about your THINKING and your WRITING, not the length. 3. Share your portfolio. Send 2–3 examples of ads, hooks, scripts, or concepts YOU wrote that ran for real brands. Drive link, Notion page, or PDF — whatever works. No portfolio = no interview. 4. Tell us: Your hourly rate (within $5–8) Your weekly availability (hours/week) Your WhatsApp number How many years you've specifically written ads, hooks, or scripts for paid social Which brands or industries you've written for One sentence: why this role specifically, not just "any job" What Happens Next If your application is strong, we send you ONE paid test brief — You write hooks, a script, and a short concept rationale. Pass that, and we book a 20-minute call. After the call, we offer a 30-day paid trial at your hourly rate. After 30 days, we either commit long-term or part ways professionally. We move fast. If we like you, you can be working within 1 week. What We're NOT Not an agency. You work with the founder directly. Not a "job mill." We hire ONE person at a time and we keep them for years. Not looking for graphic designers, video editors, or general VAs. If this sounds like the right fit — apply today. We're reviewing applications this week and hiring fast.

title: Care Coordinator Patient Chart Auditor
description: The Care Coordinator Patient Chart Auditor is responsible for conducting monthly audits of the performance of Care Coordinators. Using established audit criteria, scoring standards, and quality assurance guidelines, the chart auditor will look for compliance with company policies, documentation standards, communication expectations, and established workflow ---------- diting patient charts includes searching through Omni Therapy’s EMR platform and communication records. Audit findings are documented and shared with Account Managers to support performance monitoring and consistency across the department. This position is focused exclusively on auditing and reporting and does not include direct employee management, coaching, or disciplinary responsibilities. Essential Duties & Responsibilities Monthly Audits Conduct monthly audits of Care Coordinators’ patient charts using established audit criteria, scoring standards, and quality assurance guidelines. Review patient charts, documentation, communication logs, scheduling activity, missed visit management, discharge coordination, re-evaluation management, authorization tracking, and other assigned workflow functions. Evaluate compliance with company policies, home health agency requirements, documentation standards, communication expectations, and established workflow procedures. Verify completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and consistency of documentation and required follow-up activities. Identify deficiencies, compliance concerns, documentation gaps, workflow issues, and areas requiring follow-up. Ensure audits are completed accurately, objectively, and within established deadlines. Audit Documentation & Reporting Apply audit standards consistently and objectively across all Care Coordinators. Calculate, document, and maintain audit scores and supporting records. Maintain complete and accurate audit documentation in accordance with departmental requirements. Prepare audit summaries, score reports, and findings for Account Managers. Clearly document audit observations, deficiencies, compliance concerns, and areas requiring corrective action or follow-up. Track audit results and maintain historical audit data for performance monitoring and reporting purposes. Trend Analysis & Quality Improvement Identify recurring documentation issues, workflow deficiencies, and compliance trends across audited charts. Monitor patterns that may indicate training needs, process gaps, or operational risks. Provide data-driven insights and recommendations to support quality improvement initiatives. Assist in maintaining consistency and standardization of Care Coordinator processes across all assigned accounts. Escalate significant compliance concerns or recurring issues to Account Managers for review and action. Experience: 2+ years of experience in home health, care coordination, healthcare operations, medical records review, auditing, or a related healthcare support role. Strong understanding of care coordinator workflows, documentation requirements, scheduling processes, and home health operations preferred. Previous auditing, chart review, or quality monitoring experience is a plus. Technical Skills: Proficient with Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems (experience with Devero or similar platforms is a major plus) and communication software like RingCentral (RC). Proficient with Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets for audit tracking, reporting, and score calculations. Attention to Detail: Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to identify missing documentation, workflow gaps, compliance concerns, and inconsistencies across patient charts and communication records. Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with the ability to review documentation, identify trends, apply audit criteria consistently, and accurately score performance based on established standards. Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly document audit findings, summarize observations, and communicate audit-related information professionally and objectively. Benefits: Competitive Pay Annual Bonus Annual salary increases (Performance Based) Health Insurance Paid Holidays Paid Vacation Paid Sick Leave * Must be available to work Monday - Friday, from 9am - 5:30pm Pacific Standard Time. * Previous experience working night shift with an international company is preferred.

description: Personal Dating App Manager (Ghostwriter–Operator) I'm hiring someone to run the day-to-day of my dating profiles. You're the engine behind the scenes: curating matches, opening conversations, keeping promising ones warm, and getting the good ones to a scheduled date. I handle the actual dates — you handle everything up to them. This is fast AI-assisted drafting with light judgment, not pure copy-paste. You'll use tools to generate options quickly, but you read the thread and pick or adjust so it lands like a real person. The difference between a date and a dead conversation is usually one good reply at the unexpected ---------- nt — that's the skill I'm hiring for. Apps you'd manage: [Hinge / Bumble / Tinder / etc.] Goal: [be specific — e.g. "consistent, quality first dates with people I'd actually click with"] What you'll do Review and curate matches against a preferences brief I'll give you Write openers and carry conversations in my voice Keep ---------- ntum: timely replies, good questions, knowing when to ask someone out Handle the "message three" save — when someone says something the script didn't anticipate, you keep it alive Flag standout matches to me before any date is set Maintain a clean log of who's who so threads never cross Suggest tweaks to my photos and bio over time based on what's landing Edit and prep my profile photos — light retouching, cropping, ordering, and basic cleanup so the profile always looks its best (no heavy/deceptive editing; the photos still have to look like me) Tools & Workflow You'll operate a defined stack so the work is fast and consistent. I'll provide access and a voice brief. Drafting — YourMove AI (default engine for openers and replies). [Swap/secondary: SmoothRizz if we prioritize voice-consistency.] Match tracking — Wingman (AI Dating Coach app): a profile per person so we track what's been said and what's worked, and never cross threads. Also our photo/bio optimizer. Delivery — the actual apps, by hand. You log in and type inside [Hinge/Bumble/Tinder]. No automation or auto-senders — those get accounts banned. [Optional: Keys AI keyboard to speed up in-app typing, on the dedicated device only.] Access — 1Password (or Bitwarden): you get login access without raw credentials; I can revoke instantly. Brief & coordination — shared Notion doc: my voice, preferences, and standing rules live here. Photo editing — [Lightroom Mobile / Snapseed / Canva / TouchRetouch]: for cropping, light retouching, ordering, and cleanup. Use whichever you're fluent in; just keep edits natural. The rhythm: read the thread ? generate options ? pick the one that fits and tweak it to sound like me ? send ? log anything worth remembering. Seconds of judgment per message, not minutes of writing. Who I'm looking for A genuinely strong, natural writer with range — funny, warm, or sharp depending on the person High emotional intelligence and a good read on subtext Comfortable using AI tools to draft fast and the judgment to know when a suggestion is off Competent with basic photo editing — cropping, light retouching, and selecting the strongest shots Discreet and trustworthy — this is my actual dating life Responsive during [active hours] Bonus: you've done this kind of work before, or you're just unusually good at texting Confidentiality You'll have access to my accounts and personal conversations. A basic confidentiality agreement is part of the role — non-negotiable, and I'll provide it before any account access. How to apply — the screening I'm using a few short steps instead of a résumé, because the work is the audition. Step 1 — Quick intro + read-the-brief check (5 min). A short note answering: why does this kind of work appeal to you? Then, so I know you actually read instructions before acting: Start your message with the word "Banana." Keep the whole note under 100 words. End with one line confirming you're comfortable signing a confidentiality agreement. No cover letter — keep it human. (If you skip any of the three, I'll assume the instruction-following part of the job isn't a fit, and won't move forward. This is the filter, not a formality.) Step 2 — Work sample (writing + photo). I'll send a mock match profile and one sample photo. You'll: Write the opener you'd send them. Rewrite this bland bio to make it pull: "[insert a boring sample bio]" Do a quick, natural edit of the sample photo (crop + light cleanup) and send it back — show me you can make a shot look its best without making it look fake. Step 3 — The message-three save (the real filter). I'll give you a conversation that's gone cold, or a match who said something slightly off or unexpected. Show me how you'd recover or respond. This tells me more than anything else. Step 4 — Paid trial. Top candidates do a [1–2 week] paid trial on a live account, with me reviewing before anything sends. If it clicks, we make it ongoing. To start: reply with Step 1 and I'll send the Step 2 brief. Notes for me before posting: lock the rate and hours (vague pay attracts vague applicants — even a range sharpens the pool a lot), confirm which apps I'm listing, and run YourMove + Wingman through their free trials on my real threads first so I know the stack actually works before handing it off.

description: Paa Prefab is a growing prefab housing and building-products company on the Big Island of Hawaii. We sell prefab buildings, storage and office units, container-style spaces, and related building products for customers who need practical, affordable space. I am hiring a remote General Manager / Business Operations Manager to help run the parts of the company that need consistent follow-through, organization, reporting, research, and systems. This role is for someone who can take ownership across multiple areas of the business: finance admin, marketing coordination, sales follow-up, procurement research, customer communication, supplier tracking, project organization, and internal systems. I am looking for someone who can operate independently, solve problems, create structure, maintain standards, and make the business easier to run without needing constant hand-holding. You will work directly with the owner. Your job is to own the operating rhythm of the business, keep work moving, surface decisions clearly, and reduce the number of things that fall back on the owner. Financial, marketing, and sales as well as management success, a hunger and will to succeed, strong problem solving, and the track-record to prove it. Core Areas You Will Help Own Finance and Regulatory Admin You will help keep the business financially organized and legally in compliance of tax and other accounting requirements. This may include: • Organizing invoices, receipts, quotes, payments, and vendor records. • Researching required State, Federal Tax and other required reporting/submissions on time. • Tracking customer deposits, balances due, payment status, and follow-up needs. • Preparing simple finance summaries for owner review. • Coordinating with bookkeepers, accountants, or outside finance support. • Flagging missing documents, unpaid balances, unusual charges, or unclear records. • Helping prepare clean records for taxes, bookkeeping, and reporting. You will not be expected to make final financial decisions without approval, but you should be able to keep the finance admin side organized and visible. Sales Operations You will help make sure leads and customers do not fall through the cracks. This may include: • Managing CRM records and lead pipelines. • Tracking every lead’s status and next step. • Drafting customer replies and follow-up messages. • Preparing quote information for owner review. • Making sure customer questions get answered or escalated. • Tracking interested customers, serious buyers, quote requests, deposits, and delivery status. • Identifying which leads need urgent attention. The goal is not just to reply to messages. The goal is to help build a reliable sales follow-up system. Marketing Coordination You will help keep marketing organized and active. This may include: • Coordinating Facebook Marketplace listings and social media posts. • Organizing product photos, descriptions, pricing notes, and listing copy. • Tracking which products are listed where. • Watching competitor listings and local market pricing. • Helping draft ads, posts, flyers, email s, and simple marketing campaigns. • Tracking which marketing channels are producing leads. • Suggesting improvements based on what customers are asking about. Marketing should be practical, consistent, and safe for the business. No spam tactics, fake accounts, risky shortcuts, or sloppy public claims. Procurement and Supplier Research You will help research and organize supplier options. This may include: • Researching prefab buildings, container units, sheds, storage units, roofing systems, panels, accessories, tools, materials, and related products. • Comparing suppliers, pricing, shipping, minimum order quantities, lead times, and product specs. • Organizing supplier quotes and conversations. • Preparing comparison summaries. • Asking suppliers clear questions. • Tracking open supplier issues and follow-ups. • Helping identify better products, better margins, or better sourcing options. The goal is to help the owner make faster, better purchasing decisions. Operations and Project Coordination You will help turn messy daily business activity into clear systems. This may include: • Creating trackers, checklists, SOPs, templates, dashboards, and simple workflows. • Preparing daily and weekly owner updates. • Tracking open decisions, blockers, customer promises, supplier follow-ups, and delivery issues. • Organizing documents, photos, product details, quotes, invoices, contracts, and project records. • Keeping important information easy to find. • Noticing repeated problems and suggesting fixes. The strongest person for this role will not wait for every task to be assigned. They will notice what is missing and help create order. Looking For: Strong General Manager Traits I am looking for someone who is: • Excellent in written English. • Highly organized and reliable. • Calm under pressure. • Graceful and professional at all times, with customers, vendors, and coworkers. • A self-starter who does not need to be chased. • Comfortable owning several business areas at once. • Good at turning messy information into clear next steps. • Strong at follow-up, reminders, tracking, and documentation. • Able to maintain business standards even when things are moving quickly. • Able to make practical recommendations, not just collect information. • Comfortable making judgment calls and explaining your reasoning. • Careful with customer promises, pricing, permitting, delivery details, and anything that could create confusion. • Honest when you do not know something. • Able to work independently while keeping the owner informed. • Practical, direct, and action-oriented. The strongest candidate will think like a general manager, chief of staff, or operations lead — someone who sees what needs to happen, organizes it, and helps make it happen. Looking For: Useful Experience Direct construction experience is helpful, but it is not required. I am interested in people who have managed complexity in real business environments. Strong candidates may come from many backgrounds, including: • Operations management for a small business. • Finance admin, bookkeeping coordination, invoice tracking, or payment follow-up. • Sales operations, CRM management, lead follow-up, or quote coordination. • Marketing coordination, social media listings, Marketplace, paid ads, or local business marketing. • Procurement, supplier research, vendor management, importing, shipping, or product comparison. • Logistics, dispatch, delivery coordination, warehouse coordination, or inventory management. • Trades businesses, contractor offices, repair businesses, mechanical services, equipment rental, automotive, marine, appliance, solar, or other hands-on service businesses. • Real estate, property management, hospitality, events, or other high-pressure customer-facing operations. • Coordinating many moving parts across customers, vendors, schedules, documents, and money records. • CRM tools, Airtable, HubSpot, Notion, Trello, Linear, Google Sheets, or similar systems. • Working for a US, Australian, Canadian, or UK business. • ChatGPT or other AI tools used for real business operations. • Building trackers, dashboards, checklists, SOPs, or simple systems for a growing company. What matters most is not the exact industry. What matters is whether you can manage complexity, maintain standards, communicate clearly, and keep moving with calm, charm, and good judgment. Looking For: Work Style The business moves fast. Some things will be messy. Your job is to help make them clear. I value short, useful updates. I do not need long vague reports. I want information that helps decisions happen faster. Looking For: AI Tool Judgment I want someone who can use AI tools well, but not blindly. Good AI use means: • Using ChatGPT to draft, summarize, organize, compare, and speed up research. • Checking facts before relying on them. • Editing AI output so it sounds human, specific, and accurate. • Knowing when a customer-facing message needs owner approval. • Separating facts, assumptions, and open questions. • Never using AI as an excuse for sloppy work or for a lack of accountability for the work you do. How To Apply Please reply with: 1 A short introduction in your own words. 2 Your relevant experience. 3 Why you think you are a fit for a General Manager / Business Operations Manager role. 4 Your expected monthly salary in USD. 5 Your available working hours in Philippine time. 6 Your available overlap with Hawaii time, if you know it. 7 A specific example of a messy process, tracker, system, or workflow you improved. 8 A specific example of a time you solved a business problem without waiting for your boss to tell you every step. 9 A specific example of a time you stayed calm and effective in a fast-moving or high-pressure situation. 10 Which areas you are strongest in: finance admin, marketing, sales operations, procurement, customer follow-up, project coordination, systems, logistics, vendor management, or research. 11 What tools you are comfortable with: spreadsheets, CRM, Google Workspace, ChatGPT, Notion, Airtable, Trello, etc. Please also answer these questions: Question 1: A potential customer asks about a prefab home but gives incomplete information. I’m in Puna and need something cheap fast.” How would you reply? Question 3: You notice that leads are coming from Facebook , text messages, phone calls, and referrals, but there is no reliable system for tracking who needs follow-up. What would you build first? Question 4: You are researching a new supplier. What information would you collect before recommending whether we should consider buying from them? Question 5: Describe a business environment where you had to manage many moving parts at once. What standards did you maintain, and how did you keep things from falling through the cracks? Optional: Tell me how you currently use ChatGPT or AI tools in your work, and how you check the output before using it. Applications that are generic, copy-pasted, or obviously AI-written without personal detail will be skipped. Paid Test Task Strong applicants may be invited to complete a short paid test task before hiring. The test may include: • Creating a lead follow-up tracker. • Drafting a customer follow-up message. • Creating a quote-prep checklist. • Summarizing supplier/product options. • Writing a daily owner update. • Creating a basic finance/admin tracker for invoices, deposits, balances due, and missing records. • Recommending a simple operating system for managing leads, suppliers, quotes, marketing tasks, and follow-ups. • Explaining which customer, finance, pricing, permitting, or public-facing issues should require owner approval. I am looking for judgment, clarity, structure, independence, follow-through, calm under pressure, and practical thinking. Compensation This is a serious full-time role. Pay is USD $2,000/month for the right person. I am willing to pay well for someone who is independent, reliable, organized, calm, honest, and able to take ownership of finance admin, sales operations, marketing coordination, procurement research, logistics support, vendor follow-up, and business systems so the company can run with less owner involvement.

title: TikTok Social Media Manager — Part-Time, Philippines-Based | DTC E-Commerce Brand | $350–$550/mo
job_title: TikTok Social Media Manager — Part-Time, Philippines-Based | DTC E-Commerce Brand | $350–$550/mo
description: Is This You? You wake up and the first thing you check is your For You Page — not because you're bored, but because you're studying it. You know what's converting this week. You know which sounds are peaking. You know the difference between a hook that stops thumbs and a hook that makes people actually watch past three seconds. You've run TikTok for a real brand — not just your personal account, not just a side project. You've posted content, watched the numbers, formed a hypothesis, changed the approach, and done it again. You don't need someone to explain the algorithm to you. You need someone to let you work. If that's you, keep reading. If you're still figuring out TikTok while managing it for brands, this isn't the right fit. What You'll Own • TikTok is your primary responsibility. You'll plan, script, edit, post, and iterate on content for 3 DTC product brands in the US natural goods space — bar soap, tallow skincare, and freeze-dried pet treats. Footage comes from the brand owner and UGC creators; your job is to make it perform. Expect 2–4 posts per week per active brand, scaling as the brands grow. • Build and maintain a content calendar — and actually hit it, without being reminded. • Write hooks that compete. Every video starts with a line or a visual that earns the next three seconds. You'll be judged on this. • Select audio strategically — trending sounds, original audio, voiceover decisions. You'll know why you chose what you chose. • Structure videos for completion rate: pacing, editing rhythm, CTA placement. CapCut or similar is your tool. • Repurpose UGC and existing video assets into original-feeling content — recut, reframed, re-scored. You know how to transform raw footage so the algorithm treats it as new, not duplicate. Uncut re-uploads are not an option here. • Use native TikTok formats — Duet, Stitch, Green Screen — strategically to extend reach, respond to trends, and generate engagement without starting from zero every time. • Repurpose top-performing TikToks for Instagram Reels. Manage Facebook pages (posting, community replies, basic scheduling). • Monitor comments and DMs across platforms; flag anything that needs owner attention. • Coordinate with TikTok Shop: product link setup, affiliate outreach awareness, live selling scheduling when applicable. • Track your own metrics — reach, watch time, saves, shares, follower growth — and deliver a clear weekly summary. No vanity-metric spin. Just honest numbers and what you're doing about them. • Proactively bring content ideas, trend observations, and competitive intel to the owner. Don't wait to be asked. What We're Looking For Hard Requirements • Minimum 2 years managing TikTok for a US-market brand or agency client (product brands preferred) • Demonstrated results: you can show before/after data or real account growth you drove • Fluent written English — you'll write scripts, captions, and direct communications with the brand owner • Proficient in CapCut or equivalent mobile/desktop editing tool • Available for async communication; able to flag urgent items in real time during PH business hours • Reliable and deadline-driven — you treat posting schedules like commitments, not suggestions • Comfortable working with minimal supervision on a fully remote team Strong Advantages • TikTok Shop experience: product linking, affiliate program coordination, LIVE commerce awareness • Experience in natural products, wellness, pet, or handcrafted goods categories • Proficiency with native TikTok formats: Duet, Stitch, Green Screen — used as deliberate reach and engagement tools, not just features • Instagram Reels native editing (not just cross-posting) • Familiarity with US consumer behavior and the DTC e-commerce landscape ?? TikTok Compliance & Platform Intelligence — Non-Negotiable This section matters more than most postings acknowledge, so it gets its own block. These brands operate in regulated-adjacent categories: skincare, pet nutrition, personal care. One compliant-looking post with the wrong claim, a banned audio track, or a policy violation the owner didn't know about can cost a suppressed account, a restricted shop, or worse. We need someone who treats TikTok's Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and Commerce Policies as required reading — not fine print. That means: • You track policy updates. You know what changed in the last 90 days and what it means for product-based content. • You flag risks before posting — not after the fact. • You understand what can and cannot be said in TikTok Shop product listings, video captions, and on-screen text for health and wellness products. • You know which claim types trigger review, suppression, or removal, and you keep the brand far away from those lines. • You understand TikTok's duplicate content detection — and know how to properly re-edit, reframe, and re-score UGC or existing footage so it registers as original. Re-uploading uncut videos is a fast way to get suppressed. You don't do that. • You can explain your compliance reasoning when asked. Candidates who treat this as a checkbox will not advance. Candidates who treat this as a professional discipline will. What You'll Get • $350–$550 USD/month, part-time (~20 hours/week) — based on experience and demonstrated results. This is a part-time engagement to start, with a clear path to full-time as the brands scale. • Fully remote. Core hours are Manila time, founders live in Philippines. No micromanagement. No daily check-in calls. You own your schedule as long as deadlines are met. • Stable, long-term engagement — this is not a project hire. The right person grows with us. As posting volume increases and results compound, the scope (and pay) expands. • Clear scope. You won't be asked to do customer service, inventory, or tasks outside your lane. • Direct access to the brand owner — decisions get made fast, feedback is real, and good work gets recognized. How to Apply Send the following: 1. A brief intro (3–5 sentences): who you are, what brands or accounts you've managed on TikTok, and one result you're proud of. 2. Links to 2–3 TikTok accounts you've managed (or specific videos if the accounts are no longer live). If the work is under NDA, describe it — but be specific. 3. Your answer to this question. This is required. No answer = no consideration: "Name one TikTok rule, policy change, or platform update from the last 6 months that could affect a US e-commerce brand selling physical products. How would you handle it — both in terms of your content approach and what you'd communicate to the brand owner?" Answer in your own words. A vague, generic or AI-generated response tells us everything we need to know. These are small, real brands built around products people genuinely love. We're not filling a seat — we're looking for someone who takes pride in their work, wants a stable long-term role, and is ready to grow alongside us. If that's you, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Amazon/Walmart Product Researcher for Live Deal Website
job_title: Amazon/Walmart Product Researcher for Live Deal Website
description: I run an online deals website and deal-alert groups. I am looking for a fast, focused worker who can help find real Amazon/Walmart deals and prepare them for posting. This is not just a Shopify product listing job. The most important part of this job is finding good, post-worthy deals quickly. Main Responsibilities: Watch deal websites, Telegram channels, Amazon, Walmart, and other deal sources. Find strong Amazon/Walmart deals that are actually worth posting. Check if the price is truly good, not just “cheap.” Make sure deals are fresh/current, preferably price drops from today. Avoid old price drops, weak discounts, random junk products, and products with poor reviews. Prefer brand-name products when possible, but unknown brands can be considered if the deal is very strong, the reviews look good, and the product is useful. Avoid niche replacement parts or accessories that only work if someone already owns a specific product. Check if we posted the same or similar product recently. Prepare deals quickly with a clean title, sale price, regular price, coupon info, and clear instructions. Post deals to Shopify and share them to WhatsApp/social media. Work fast and stay focused during the full shift. What I Need: I need someone with strong deal judgment. You must understand the difference between a cheap product and a real deal. A good deal is usually a useful, complete product with a fresh price drop, strong discount, good reviews/brand, and real value for our audience. I do not want random junk, niche replacement parts, old price drops, weak discounts, or products that only a few people can use. Brand-name products are preferred, but unknown brands are okay when the discount is very strong, the reviews look good, and there are no better deals available. A strong deal can be: 50% off or more on a useful product 70% off or more on a very strong deal Sometimes 30% off if it is a popular brand, expensive item, household item, toy, clothing, baby item, electronics, or something people regularly buy But the discount must be real and the product must be worth posting. This job is not about sending many random links. Weak deals do not count. I need quality and speed together. Important Performance Expectations: When deal sources are active, I expect steady output. The target is around 10–16 quality deal submissions per hour, depending on how active the sources are. Sending only 4–5 deals per hour is usually not enough when other deal sites are actively posting. Sending many weak/junk deals just to show quantity is not acceptable. I would rather get 8 strong deals than 20 bad ones. Before sending/posting a deal, check that the price, coupon, promo code, and discount are still working now. Good Experience To Have: Please mention if you have experience with any of these: Amazon product research Walmart product research Keepa Online arbitrage Retail arbitrage Amazon FBA product sourcing Shopify product posting Affiliate/deal websites Telegram or ---------- deal posting Social media posting Direct deal-hunting experience is a big plus, but it is not required if you are smart, fast, focused, and willing to learn. Required Skills: Fast computer skills Good English reading and writing Strong attention to detail Ability to work without constant reminders Good product judgment Ability to follow instructions exactly Fast response time Reliable attendance Focused work during shift hours Work Hours: All hours are in U.S. New York Time Zone. These hours are non-negotiable. Sunday: 2:30 PM – 10:30 PM Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday: 4:30 PM – 10:30 PM, sometimes until 11:00 PM Saturday night in winter: around 6:30 PM – 11:30 PM Saturday night in summer: around 9:30 PM – 11:30 PM or 11:45 PM Internet, Power, and Backup Requirements: Because this is a live deal-alert job, reliable attendance and connection are very important. You must have: Stable home internet Backup internet, such as mobile hotspot or a second internet option Backup power, such as a generator, power station, or UPS A work location with limited power outages/blackouts Ability to stay online during the full shift without frequent disconnections Please do not apply if you regularly lose power or internet during work hours. Phone Requirement: You must have a good, up-to-date smartphone with fast mobile internet. Your phone must be able to: Run WhatsApp, Telegram , Shopify, browser, and social media apps smoothly Receive and send deal alerts quickly Be used as a mobile hotspot if home internet goes down Stay charged during the full shift Handle fast posting without freezing or lagging Trial Test: Before hiring, I will give a paid trial task. You may be asked to review deal links and choose which ones are worth posting, which ones should be skipped, and explain why. I am looking for someone who can think like this: “This is a good brand.” “This discount is strong.” “This product is useful for families.” “This looks cheap but it is junk.” “This is only a replacement part, so I would skip it.” “This was probably posted recently.” “This should be posted now before it sells out.” Starting pay: $3.25/hour during trial. Pay can increase to $3.50/hour after 12–14 weeks based on speed, deal quality, accuracy, focus, and attendance. Bonuses available for excellent performance. Bonuses may be available for excellent performance in busy seasons. We also provide one week of paid vacation twice per year. To Apply: Please answer these questions: 1) Have you done Amazon, Walmart, Keepa, online arbitrage, product research, or deal research before? 2) What tools have you used? 3) How fast can you work while staying accurate? 4) Are you comfortable being measured by both speed and quality? 5) Are you available to work the hours listed above in U.S. New York Time? 6) What phone model do you use? 7) Do you have fast mobile data? 8) Can your phone be used as a hotspot if your home internet goes down? 9) Please send a screenshot of your home internet speed test. 10) Please send a screenshot of your mobile internet speed test. 11) What is your backup internet option? 12) What is your backup power option? 13) How often do you usually have power outages or internet problems? 14)What city/province in the Philippines do you work from? Send one example of a product you think is a strong deal and explain why. Please do not apply if you only want a simple copy/paste job. I need someone who can find quality deals fast and stay focused.

title: Strategic Project Manager – EV Infrastructure & Vehicle Inspection
job_title: Strategic Project Manager – EV Infrastructure & Vehicle Inspection
description: Job Summary: We are seeking an analytical, process-driven Strategic Project Manager to act as the primary gatekeeper and operational architect for our upcoming initiatives. In this role, you will evaluate incoming opportunities in the EV charging station and vehicle inspection spaces, analyzing them against our strategic goals and past performance to determine viability ("Should we pursue this project?"). You won't just manage timelines—you will be responsible for deconstructing complex project scopes, identifying technical and utility requirements, reviewing or creating winning commercial proposals, and designing step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). The ideal candidate combines a background in technical project management (infrastructure, utilities, or fleet operations) with a rigorous approach to process standardisation. Key Responsibilities: 1. Project Evaluation & Feasibility Analysis (Go/No-Go) Critically evaluate new project leads for charging station installations and vehicle inspection programs to assess financial profitability, technical viability, and operational capacity. Review prospective station sites or fleet sizes against our historical data to advise leadership on whether a project makes strategic sense to pursue. Factor in variables like utility grid capacity, local zoning laws, inspection volume, and regional compliance factors during initial evaluation phases. 2. Technical Scope Breakdown & Requirements Gathering Deconstruct high-level project requests into highly technical, executable project scopes. Map out exact requirements for EV charging deployment (e.g., electrical load demands, transformer upgrades, hardware/software interoperability, ADA compliance). Identify exact criteria for vehicle inspection setups (e.g., diagnostic tool integration, physical lane layouts, safety testing compliance, data management systems). Pinpoint project bottlenecks, supply chain constraints (hardware lead times), and permitting risks early on. 3. Proposal Creation & Review Draft thorough, professional project proposals, Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and Statements of Work (SOWs) for clients, municipal entities, or enterprise fleet partners. Conduct strict reviews of internally created proposals to ensure cost estimates, deployment timelines, and resource allocations are realistic and protect the company from scope creep. 4. Process Optimization & SOP Development Build out a library of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for newly approved projects to ensure seamless, highly repeatable field execution. Author SOPs for charging station installation, site commissioning, safety testing, and post-install maintenance. Create standardized workflows, inspection checklists, and software training SOPs for vehicle inspection technicians to ensure quality control and regulatory compliance. Qualifications & Experience: Experience: 4+ years of project management or operations management experience, specifically within EV charging infrastructure, civil/electrical construction, fleet management, or automotive service/inspection programs. Analytical Assessment: Strong ability to read technical site plans, utility sheets, or fleet specifications and make data-driven decisions on project feasibility. Documentation Excellence: Proven track record of drafting complex proposals, SOWs, and creating highly structured, clear SOPs for technical workflows. Regulatory/Technical Knowledge: * Familiarity with EV charging infrastructure (Level 2 & DC Fast Charging, utility interconnection, permitting). Familiarity with automotive/vehicle inspection standards, diagnostic equipment, or compliance regulations is a major asset. Tools: Proficiency with project management platforms (e.g., ClickUp, Asana, Jira, Monday.com) and visual process mapping tools (e.g., Lucidchart, Miro). Certification: PMP, Lean Six Sigma (Green or Black Belt), or CAPM is highly preferred. Who You Are: The Strategic Gatekeeper: You know how to look past the excitement of a new deal and evaluate whether it actually makes financial and operational sense for the team to execute. Detail-Obsessed: You care about the nuance of a utility grid connection or the exact calibration steps of a vehicle inspection tool, ensuring no detail is missed in the scope. A Process Creator: You thrive on turning a chaotic, "one-off" project execution into a repeatable, step-by-step SOP system that anyone on the team can follow. An Effective Communicator: You can easily align utility companies, electrical contractors, inspection technicians, and executive stakeholders on a singular vision.

title: Executive Assistant to the Founder
description: Good work should win the work. Rootl helps tradespeople and local service businesses get found, picked and booked online. We exist because good businesses lose to worse ones every day. Not because they are worse at the job, but because the worse ones got found first. It started with advice from an upstairs window to a window cleaner halfway up a ladder. By 2036 we want Rootl to be the UK's most trusted local search company for trades and local service businesses, with our first US hub open. We are building the team that gets us there. Want a seat on the bus? ## WHAT WE DO We help tradespeople and local service businesses get found on Google, and inside the AI tools their next customer is already searching with: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini. That is the job. We do it for plumbers, electricians, roofers, joiners, waste firms, architects, developers, and the trades around them. Three core services, one job done properly: getting our clients found when their next customer is looking. We are a small, growing team. The founder runs sales and strategy. A web developer builds the client sites. A content operations manager runs the content. This new seat is the founder's right hand, the person who holds everything together so the rest of us can do our jobs. ## THE ROLE, IN ONE LINE You protect the founder's time and turn what is in his head into a system the business can run on. ## ABOUT THIS SEAT This is the founder's right hand. The person who holds the structure, protects the time, and takes the mental load so the founder can focus on growing the business. ## READ THIS TWICE The next part is the honest version. Read it carefully, because it tells you exactly what you would be walking into. ## A STRAIGHT WORD, FOUNDER TO YOU I have never hired someone into this seat before. For two years I have run this business out of my own head. The inbox, the calendar, the onboarding, the follow-ups, the systems, all of it lives in my memory and on my plate. It has got me this far. It will not get me where we are going. I know that to scale this business I have to get the mentalness out of my head and into a system someone else can run. That is the job. You are not walking into a finished machine. You are helping me build it, then helping me let go of it. So be clear on what you are walking into. I move fast. I set twelve things going in a week and I need someone to catch the three that fell. Some weeks will feel like organised chaos. This role exists to bring order to it. If that excites you rather than worries you, this is your seat. It is a rocket ship, and I want you on it. ## WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE Here is the real test, and it comes from my corporate days before Rootl. I had an emergency appendectomy three days before a major event in San Diego that I was running. I could not fly. So I wrote up a full handover plan and passed it to my boss from the back of the car while my replacement was on their way to the airport. The event ran without me, because everything they needed was written down. That is what winning looks like in this seat. If I take an afternoon off, or a week off, the system runs itself. You are the person who makes that true, by turning what is in my head into something written down that anyone can pick up. There is a second, quieter version of success, and it happens every single day. You become the gateway. I have taken email off my phone and handed the inbox to you. You manage my calendar, not me. I do not always know what is coming up next week, because I do not need to. You do. I trust the surface you show me to be right, and that trust is the whole point of the seat. ## TRUST AND CONFIDENTIALITY This is the part that matters most, so read it carefully. This seat sees things almost no one else does. My inbox, my calendar, the numbers, the decisions, the conversations I would not have anywhere else. The role only works on a foundation of complete trust. We need someone with a high degree of integrity, discretion, and confidentiality. What you see in this seat stays in this seat. This is written into the contract as the first clause, and we will talk about it openly at interview, because it is not a detail. It is the ground the whole role stands on. ## WHY YOU'D WANT THIS SEAT - A real seat at the table. You work closely with the founder, you are the eyes and ears across the team, and you are someone I can bat ideas off. This is not a fetch-and-carry role. - A clear lane that is yours. I run sales, marketing and strategy. Our web developer builds the sites. Our content manager runs the content engine. You hold the operation together and protect my time. Everyone knows their seat, and this one is yours. - Responsibility from day one. Not a six-month shadow. - You help write the process, not just follow it. Using the founder's own recordings (camcorder method), voice notes, and you build the SOPs every future Rootl hire is trained on. - Variety with depth. You will do a range of things, and you will also do similar things well and make them tighter each time. - Real long-term upside for the person who stays the course. We will talk that through properly once you are established. - The local search world is shifting under everyone's feet right now. You will be close to the front of it. - We hire the right person, not the perfect person. Every candidate is DISC profiled, because the seat has to fit how we work. ## WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Inbox and calendar. You filter the inbox, surface only what I need, and protect my diary. I do not want email on my phone. That is your world. - Helping me plan the week. What is scheduled, what can be pushed, what matters most. You are the person I benchmark against so I feel organised. - Meeting prep and follow-ups. Getting me ready before a call, and making sure nothing drops after it. - Marketing and offers admin. Organising campaigns, drafting offers from my rough notes, and crafting my weekly Thursday networking pitch with other business owners so I can review and rehearse it. - Client onboarding, owned end to end. Intake form, welcome email , CRM setup, contract back-end, getting people access to systems. One repeatable process, run the same way every time. - Sales support. Scheduling the inbound enquiries and DMs that come from our campaigns, running first-pass research on a prospect against our fit benchmark and handing me a profile sheet before the call, and chasing proposals through to a yes or a clean no. - Team conduit. Keeping Slack current and Notion up to date, documenting decisions as they happen, and holding our weekly team rhythm with the rest of the team. - System building. Working with me to document one process every week, so the business stops living in my head. - Tool stand-up. Owning the setup when a new system comes in: project boards, pipelines, trackers, CRM updates. There will also be ad hoc tasks. This seat suits someone who enjoys variety and likes being the person who keeps an eye on how things are running across the team. ## HOW THIS SEAT THINKS This is the standard I am building toward, and it is how I want this seat held from day one. These five run underneath everything above. - Protect my time. You filter what comes in and d ---------- what actually needs me. Most things do not. Guarding my time and attention is the first job, and everything else sits under it. - Prioritise revenue. When everything feels urgent, you sort by what makes money or saves money first. That is the tie-breaker. The task that protects a client or wins a job comes before the one that just shouts loudest. - Design the play. You come prepared and you think ahead. You see the thing coming before it lands on me, and you have already worked out the options. You plan the week, the meeting, and the follow-up before I have to ask. - Answer everyone well. Every message gets a clear, kind reply, even when the answer is no. How we treat people is how we are remembered, and you are often the first voice they hear from Rootl. - Keep the calendar clean and clear. Every entry has the context I need to walk into it cold. Who, what, why, and what I need to have ready. No naked invites, no guessing, no surprises. ## WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR - You love systems. You see a messy process and you want to make it clean and repeatable. - You are a strong planner. Detail is your thing. You enjoy mapping out how something will run before it runs. - You are analytical and you will push back when something does not add up. Not on the person, on the logic. I want someone who tells me when I am wrong. - You are calm in chaos. A founder still building the rail does not rattle you. You bring order without needing everything to be tidy first. - You are good with people and relationships. You become the eyes and ears of the team without anyone feeling watched. - You are comfortable with ambiguity. This seat is being built as it runs, and you are helping to build it. - You take pride in doing similar work to a high standard, week in, week out, and improving it as you go. - Excellent written English. We will test this. Nice to have, not essential: - A bit of technical appetite. Comfort with tools like Zapier, simple automations, or project planning software. - Experience supporting a founder or senior leader directly. - Experience editing AI-written content to a publish-ready standard. - A handy eye for social content. If you know your way around Canva and can keep a light hand on the quality of social posts going out to local groups, that is a real plus. We have someone producing the content, but having an in-house person who knows the business well enough to sense-check it is genuinely useful. - A systems-and-time way of thinking. If you have read books like Buy Back Your Time by Dan Martell, The E-Myth by Michael E. Gerber, or you naturally think about how to protect a founder's time and turn chaos into a repeatable system, that is a real plus. It means we already speak the same language. ## HOW THIS SEAT WORKS WITH THE FOUNDER I run hot and fast. I set a lot in motion and I need someone to hold the structure underneath it. I use the word "comfortable" when I am settling for less than I should, and I say "it's in my head" when I mean I have not written it down yet. I race to the destination before the scaffolding exists, which is sometimes my greatest strength and sometimes my biggest risk. Your job is the pause valve, not the brake. You do not slow me down. You make sure the path exists for me to run on. Come to me with goals and a plan, never empty-handed. Hit your deadlines. Hold closure on decisions, because leaving things hanging is the thing I find hardest. I am direct, I am honest, and I will tell you what is on my mind. I am looking for someone who can do the same. ## TOOLS YOU WILL USE Google Workspace, Notion, Slack, HighLevel, Toggl, and AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. I am already teaching AI to write in my voice, so you will be editing and shaping output, not starting from a blank page. Experience with Zapier and automation tools are a bonus. Training and SOPs provided. You do not need every tool on day one, but you do need to learn fast. ## HOURS, PAY AND HOW IT WORKS - Part-time to start, around 10 hours a week, paid at $10 USD an hour. Hours grow toward 20 a week within the first 90 days as we find our rhythm and as I hand more over. - We start with a short unpaid test task so we can see how you work. If it goes well, you move onto a paid trial, paid for the hours you actually work. - Your hours and your rate both grow as you prove yourself and as the business grows. The aim is to build this into a senior, long-term seat for the right person. - If the work ever drops, we give you at least one week's written notice of any change to your hours. - Paid weekly for your first month, then monthly after that, by Wise. - You track your time in Toggl. Your tracked hours are what you invoice, so it stays clear and fair on both sides. - Every Monday we run a 30-minute tea ---------- eting using the LIONS sheet: last week, issues, opportunities, the next seven days, and successes. You fill yours in and come ready to run your part. - Most mornings we jump on a quick 15-minute call to set up the day, what matters, what is moving, what I need from you. A slightly longer one at the start of the week to plan it out. This daily contact is how the seat works, so you need to be someone who is happy with that rhythm. - I try to work UK hours, 7:00 to 4:30. At least half your hours each week need to fall inside that window so we can work together properly. For you in the Philippines that is roughly 2pm to 11:30pm, so an evening pattern fits well. - This is an independent contractor role on a proper written agreement covering confidentiality, client data, and how we pay you. You look after your own taxes in the Philippines, and you provide your own computer, reliable internet, and a quiet place to work. - Four weeks' notice on either side if it is ever not working out. ## THE HIRING PROCESS We want this to be clear and fair, so here is exactly how it runs. Everything up to the offer is unpaid, and the test task is the same for everyone. 1. You apply (opening with the screening phrase below). 2. We shortlist. 3. We send you a short test task with a clear deadline. 4. You complete and return it. 5. We score it and shortlist again. 6. You complete a DISC profile (a short questionnaire, so we understand how you work). 7. You have an interview with the founder. 8. If it is a yes on both sides, we make a provisional offer: a paid trial of one to two weeks, paid for the hours you work. 9. If the trial goes well, we move into a longer arrangement. ## HOW TO APPLY - Start your application with the phrase "Save me a seat" so we know you have read this far. - Tell us, in a few lines, about a time you took something chaotic off someone's plate and made it run smoothly. - Tell us about a system or process you built or improved, and what changed because of it. - Share any examples of executive support, admin, or operations work you are proud of. - The test task, when it comes, will be a real early-morning brain dump from the founder, for you to sort, prioritise, and turn into a clear plan. Unpaid, and the same for everyone. ## A LAST WORD We are not the biggest name out there, and we are not trying to be, (yet!) We are building something properly, and this seat is fundamental to getting it right. If you have read this far and something here lit you up, that is a good sign. Show us why it should be you. Want a seat on the bus?
